newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL ponders alternative Eurotunnel plans.
newsitem.headline: DHL ponders alternative Eurotunnel plans.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it was considering introducing contingency plans for its cross-Channel trucking service following the suspension of Eurotunnel's freight shuttles as a result of a fire late on Monday.
DHL operates scheduled overnight trucking services from its London distribution centre and Paris/Charles de Gaulle airport, Brussels and Breda (Holland).

"Luckily for us, the fire occured at a time when none of our vehicles were in the tunnel and secondly, on a Monday night when we have a reduced cross-Channel service," DHL's network planning manager, Europe-Middle East/Africa, Malcolm Macbeth, told Reuters.
On most evenings DHL uses the Eurotunnel for six nightly routes in each direction between London and Paris/CDG, Brussels and Breda using a fleet of vans, light trucks and HGVs, Macbeth said.
"We are going to play it by ear until later in the day and then if necessary, make alternative arrangements."
A likely option would be to put on an extra flight between London Heathrow and Brussels using a small aircraft, Macbeth added.
"Certainly, the volume we truck through the tunnel represents a reasonable plane-load."
DHL operates scheduled Boeing 727F services between London and Brussels and Luton and the Belgian capital.
The tunnel fire broke out at 21.45 Monday evening on a France-U.K. freight shuttle run, a Eurotunnel official said.
"We hope to resume Eurostar passenger services late this afternoon followed by freight trains. However, it remains very doubtful that freight shuttle services will be resumed today (Tuesday)."
According to latest reports, around 15 burnt out trucks have yet to be evacuated from the Tunnel where the fire took place, the official added.
Eurotunnel freight personnel were in contact with customers keeping them informed of developments. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
